study_name.evidence_quote: Tett et al., 2019, Cell Host & Microbe 26, 666–679
study_name.notes: Canonical study name constructed from first author surname (Tett, A.) and publication year (2019); not stated verbatim as a study identifier.

subject_id.notes: No individual subject-level identifiers are given; only aggregate demographic statistics per country/age-group are reported.

sample_id.notes: No per-sample identifiers provided in the accessible text; sample metadata tables (Table S1, S2, S5) are referenced but their contents are not included in the provided text.

pmid.notes: PMID provided as external paper_id; not found verbatim within the extracted text body.

subcohort.evidence_quote: We also sequenced two non-Westernized populations from Ghana and Tanzania.
subcohort.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
subcohort.notes: Subcohorts defined by country and adult/child-infant age split as reported in Experimental Model and Subject Details.

target_condition.notes: Study subjects were healthy, free of self-reported disease; the study focuses on microbial (P. copri) population structure rather than a disease phenotype.

control.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
control.notes: No case-control comparison was performed for the Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohorts; they represent a population survey, not disease cases/controls.

country.evidence_quote: For Ghana, 44 individuals were included... For Ethiopia 50 individuals... And for Tanzania 68 individuals

body_site.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from a Ghanaian cohort
body_site.notes: Same body site (feces) applies to Ghanaian, Ethiopian, and Tanzanian cohorts.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: the local occupation is subsistence farming and the wider economy based on farming cash crops such as cocoa and plantain
lifestyle.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
lifestyle.notes: Ethiopian cohort occupation/lifestyle type not explicitly described beyond being non-Westernized.

location.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families from the Asante Akim North district region were sampled
location.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets

westernized.evidence_quote: we also sequenced two non-Westernized populations from Ghana and Tanzania
westernized.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
westernized.notes: Applies to Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts, all classified as non-Westernized.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: For all samples DNA was extracted using the PowerSoil DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) as previously described
dna_extraction_kit.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Applies to Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq2500 100nt paired end platform with a target depth of 5Gb/sample
sequencing_platform.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
sequencing_platform.notes: Applies to Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts.

age.notes: Average ages per country/age-group subgroup; these are aggregate means, not individual subject ages.

age_group.notes: Age group labels (adult/children/infants) are as reported by authors, though some ranges span multiple standard age-group definitions (e.g., Ghana/Tanzania 'children' groups include ages 0-15/0-18).

family.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families from the Asante Akim North district region were sampled
family.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family.notes: Extended family sampling reported for Ghana (12 families) and Tanzania (18 families) and mother-infant pairs for Ethiopia (24 families), but no individual family identifiers are given.

family_role.evidence_quote: This cohort included 24 mothers and their infant(s) for a total of 50 metagenomes.
family_role.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family_role.notes: Ghana and Tanzania cohorts are described as 'extended families' with adults/children split but without explicit parent/child role labeling.

sex.notes: Sex is reported as population-level percentages per subgroup (e.g., Ghana adults 52.2% female/47.8% male; Ethiopia adults 100% female; Tanzania adults 48.65% female/51.35% male), not as a single per-subject enum value, so cannot be assigned as a single sex value.

age_min.notes: Age ranges reported per cohort/age-group subgroup.

age_max.notes: Age ranges reported per cohort/age-group subgroup.

age_years.notes: Mean age (avg) reported per subgroup with s.d.; individual-level ages not available.

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease.notes: Applies uniformly to all Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohort subgroups.

disease_details.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.

feces_phenotype.notes: Fecal samples were collected but no specific stool phenotype/clinical measurement reported.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Although Ethiopian infants (0.167-4.5 yrs) were sampled with mothers, no feeding method details given.

obgyn_lactating.notes: Ethiopian mothers of infants are likely lactating but this is not explicitly stated.

biomarker_name.notes: No clinical biomarker panel (e.g., serum/blood biomarker) data reported; paper is a genomic/metagenomic study of P. copri.

disease_response_os.notes: No survival/outcome data reported; study does not follow disease patients for survival endpoints.

ecog_performance_status.notes: No ECOG performance status assessment reported.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal samples were collected and used for metagenomic sequencing, but no quantitative 'feces phenotype' measurement values (e.g., Bristol stool scale) are reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: No tumor size data reported; disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, IBD etc.) were analyzed only for P. copri prevalence/abundance association, not tumor measurements.

uncurated_metadata.notes: No additional free-text metadata fields beyond those captured; demographic details (age, sex) for Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohorts are reported in Experimental Model and Subject Details but do not map to a defined uncurated_metadata field beyond study_level demographic notes.

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a frequent inhabitant of the human intestinal microbiome, and it displays a large inter-individual variation
host_species.notes: Study subjects were human participants from Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania and other public human metagenomic datasets, plus ancient human (Iceman, coprolite) samples.

extraction_warnings: No per-sample or per-subject rows were available in the provided text; only aggregate demographic statistics for three newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) were reported in the Experimental Model and Subject Details section.
Supplementary tables referenced (Table S1, S2, S4, S5) which likely contain sample-level metadata were not included in the provided text (only supplementary file cover/title pages were given).
Sex was reported only as population percentages per subgroup, not as individual values, so the 'sex' field could not be populated with a single enum value.
Granularity was set to subgroup_level using country x age-group (adult/child/infant) combinations as subgroups, since these are the most specific units for which values are reported.

target_condition and control fields were set to not_reported/Not Used because the newly sequenced cohorts represent a healthy population survey rather than a case-control disease study; the paper's separate meta-analysis of disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, hypertension, cirrhosis, IBD) used previously published external datasets not described with participant-level metadata in this text.

This paper is primarily a genomic/metagenomic population-structure study of Prevotella copri; most clinical/host-phenotype schema fields (zygosity, BMI, antibiotics, dietary restriction, HLA, smoking, treatment, tumor staging, obstetric/gynecologic, neonatal details) are not reported.

Demographic data (age, sex composition, sample size) are only reported at the subgroup level (per country and adult/child-infant age-group), not per individual, so age fields are provided as subgroup aggregates (mean, s.d., range) rather than sample-level rows.
Disease/health status ('Healthy') is uniformly stated for all newly sequenced Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohort participants but is not individually itemized.

The paper's main disease-association analyses (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) refer to previously published external datasets analyzed in aggregate for clade prevalence/abundance, not to individual-level clinical metadata extractable per this schema.

No supplementary table with per-sample clinical/host metadata matching the schema fields was included in the provided text (Table S1, S2, S4, S5 references exist but their content/rows were not provided).

This paper is a microbial genomics/metagenomics study of Prevotella copri and does not report clinical biomarker, survival, ECOG, or tumor size data as defined by the schema; most fields are not_reported.

Detailed demographic data (age, sex, sample sizes) for Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohorts exist in 'Experimental Model and Subject Details' but do not correspond to any schema field other than host_species, so they were not extracted into uncurated_metadata to avoid fabricating a mapping.

No subgroup-level stratification applicable to the schema's fields was found; granularity set to study_level despite the paper containing many clade/cohort-level metagenomic comparisons (not covered by schema).
